the gestational changes of the human myometrial oxytocin receptors may be due to an increase in the number of receptors as well as an increase in the affinity of the receptors to oxytocin.
The gestational increase of human myometrial oxytocin receptor binding is due to an increase in the number of receptor binding sites.

1) the oxytocin receptor concentration in the human myo- metrium increases from nonpregnancy to first trimester and then to term; 2) the oxytocine receptor dissociation constant is lower in term than in nonpregnancy and first trimester myometrium; 3) oxytocin binding is decreased after the onset of term labor, due to the decrease of oxytocin binding sites.

the increase in the uterine sensitivity during gestation is due to the gestational increase in the OT binding sites and its affinity.
the gestational changes in the human myo-uterus are due to the gestational changes of the myometrial oxytocin receptors.

gestational increase in uterine sensitivity for OT is due to an increased number of binding sites and a higher affinity of the binding sites for OT, whereas the onset of labor is due to a marked decrease in the number but not the affinity of the binding site for OT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OT and its receptors are important factors in the regulation of human myometrial activity.
OT binding to its specific receptors increases during the gestation, reaches the highest level at term and decreases during labor.

oxytocin is an important regulator of the uterine smooth muscle and is involved in the onset and progression of uterine contractions.
